Backtest sweeps (BTS)

2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22

4536 configs: concentration_cap × risk_aversion (λ) × optimizer_lookback (441 combinations) replayed across all 7 max_watchlist_size curation sets, plus min_trade_size_frac swept as a 4th axis on the canonical watchlist (6 values). All 7 watchlist sizes are the SAME geosplit thesis (one coherent curation family), so cross-size comparisons in plots 1-3 are clean. These knobs touch only the mean-variance replay, not the curator, so the whole grid costs $0 (no LLM — the curations already exist; only expanding max_watchlist_size itself, section 11, re-curates). Metrics are benchmark-relative: Information Ratio = annualized active return ÷ tracking error vs SPY (consistency of beating the benchmark). SPY returned +71% over the window. ★ = best in column.

Look-ahead-clean. The compounder gridsearch on the geosplit curations: the curator read archived Wayback ledes where available (~46% of articles) else title-only, with the biased live ledes ignored, so each rebalance saw only period-correct news. Sections needing more curations (news_lookback §12, and the single-model LLM comparison §13-14, blind judge §15) are omitted for now. Canonical config: mws 20 / cap 0.333 / λ 4.0 / 30d. All in-sample — these rank candidates to forward-test, not an optimum.

Parameter settings

The four FREE swept knobs (every combination on the canonical watchlist = 2268 configs) and the values considered. min_trade_size_frac is swept only on the canonical watchlist (mws 20); every other size is held at its live value. All other optimizer / backtest params are held at the investor_profile.md values — these knobs only re-weight the same curations.

1. Return vs drawdown

The horizontal axis is max drawdown — the portfolio's biggest peak-to-trough loss as a fraction of its running peak (the single worst high-to-low decline over the window); further right = deeper loss. The vertical axis is annualized return, so upper-left is best (high return, shallow drawdown). Each point is one cap/λ/lookback config; color = max_watchlist_size (4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 shown), so every watchlist size contributes its own 441-config cloud (total 3087 points; min_trade pinned to the live 0.05 here — it is swept separately in section 9). Within a cloud the free knobs move a point deterministically; jumping between colors ALSO swaps the underlying curation, and those kimi re-curations swing 2-5× on their own — so read cross-color separation as parameter effect + curation-draw noise, not a clean mws response. The canonical live config (watchlist 20) is the black star.

2. Return vs L1 churn

Same points (all watchlist sizes), risk axis replaced by L1 churn = annualized one-way turnover (%/yr): how much of the portfolio is traded per year (Σ|Δweight| from share changes; drift between rebalances is not a trade). 100%/yr = the whole book turned over once a year. This is the industry-standard churn measure. Trading is free in an IRA, so read it as stability/robustness, not cost: lower churn = less noise-chasing / less overfit, so upper-left (high return, low churn) is the sweet spot. Current config: 1273%/yr.

3. Return vs L2 course correction

Same idea, but churn is the L2 (Euclidean) path length the portfolio was dragged along through weight-space (√Σ Δweight² per rebalance, summed & annualized) — your “total course-correction”. Vs L1, it weights concentrated single-name rotations more heavily. It ranks these configs almost identically to L1 (correlation 0.95), which is the useful takeaway: the two norms agree, so the churn ordering is robust. Current config: 1302/yr.

4. Recommended settings

Read straight off plots 1-3: keep only configs in the safe corner — |maxDD| < 40% AND L1 < 700 AND L2 < 900 (shallow drawdown, low churn on both norms). 776 of 4536 configs survive (by watchlist size — 4:132, 6:127, 8:91, 12:97, 16:99, 20:185, 24:45), listed once, sorted by IR. ★ = best in that column among the survivors, so you can eyeball the top IR / t-stat / Sharpe / Calmar / ann / shallowest-DD without re-sorting. min_trade_size_frac is swept as a 4th axis on the canonical watchlist (mws 20); every other size is held at the live 0.05. These stay in-sample — a forward-test shortlist, not an auto-switch. Note the live config (ws 20 0.33/4.0/30d/mt 0.05, dd 34% / L1 1273 / L2 1302) is excluded — fails L1 1273 ≥ 700, L2 1302 ≥ 900.

5. Backtest gems

Gem scan not yet run(scripts/gems_scan.py writes data/curator_runs/_gems.json).

6. Total return vs optimizer lookback (live config)

A FREE math-replay slice (no re-curation): hold the live watchlist size (20), cap (0.333) and λ (4.0) fixed and vary only the optimizer lookback (trailing days of prices used to estimate μ/Σ). The green bar is the live setting (30d).

7. Total return vs concentration_cap (live config)

Same slice, holding the live watchlist size (20), λ (4.0) and lookback (30d) fixed and varying only the concentration_cap (the per-position max weight). The green bar is the live setting (0.333).

8. Total return vs risk_aversion (live config)

Same slice, holding the live watchlist size (20), cap (0.333) and lookback (30d) fixed and varying only the risk_aversion λ (higher λ = more risk-averse = less concentrated). The green bar is the live setting (λ 4.0).

9. Total return vs min_trade_size_frac (live config)

A FREE math-replay slice (no re-curation): hold the live cap (0.333), λ (4.0), lookback (30d) fixed and vary only the no-trade band — the smallest rebalancing trade the backtest executes, as a fraction of the book. A suppressed trade's dollars are redistributed across the trades that DO clear the band, so the book stays fully invested (Fidelity IRA = zero cost, so no cost model). The green bar is the live setting (0.05). A small band can slightly improve return (avoiding whipsaw); too large a band (≥0.15) starves the momentum signal.

10. Portfolio value over time — by max_watchlist_size (vs buy/hold and SPY)

Each re-curated watchlist cap's realized portfolio value on the same pools and starter — the equity-curve view of the section-9 sweep. Tighter (smaller) watchlists concentrate into the top picks; wider ones dilute across more next-wave names.

11. max_watchlist_size sweep

Unlike the cap/λ/lookback knobs above (free math replays on one curation set), max_watchlist_size changes the curator's decisions, so each cap is a separate re-curation (~$0.40 LLM each) on the same news pools and AAPL/GOOGL/AMZN starter. The bar is each curation's total return; the QUBT / RKLB / NVDA columns flag whether that curation ever added those tickers (yes = entered the watchlist; proposed-rejected = tried but blocked).

adds/removes = the curator's proposals that the validator APPLIED; rejects = proposals still blocked after retries (double-add, add to a full watchlist with no paired remove, or a stale remove); retries = reject-and-retry rounds fired (the validator told the curator why a proposal was rejected and it re-proposed). Rejects should be ~0; retries shows how much correction that took. A large reject count means decisions are being silently blocked (the symptom that exposed the max_watchlist_size cap-override bug).
